text:
The biggest story in the Atlantic is in Tampa. On Oct. 30, Nikita Kucherov told the Lightning he won't re-sign and asked for a trade, the same week he became the franchise's career scoring leader. General manager Julien BriseBois answered publicly that the team has no intention of trading him, and Andrei Vasilevskiy, in TSN's headline, said he hopes "that something will change." Kucherov's response: six points in his last two games, including a hat trick in an 8-3 win in Buffalo.

The team around the drama is very good. Jon Cooper's Lightning are 13-4-2 with 28 points and take 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against). They have a 50% chance at the division in our simulations. They have scored about six and a half more goals than their chances predicted, so some of the 74 goals is hot finishing, and our numbers put them about four points ahead of their play.

The injuries are starting to bite. Brayden Point went on injured reserve after leaving Sunday's loss to Winnipeg, which opened the door for Sam O'Reilly, who had a point in his NHL debut; Erik Cernak and Anthony Cirelli sat out Thursday. Jake Guentzel has ten points in his last five.

Depth has been the quiet strength. Zemgus Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev have outscored opponents 10-4. The question isn't whether Tampa is good. It's whether a contender can live with its best player's exit plan hanging over every game.
headline: Kucherov wants out, and keeps winning anyway
